description: deixis-core identity vectors — the lifted equality of docs/TREE.md. Hand-authored from the spec, not generated by an implementation. Nodes are spelled over the fixture setoid of vectors/README.md: leaves carry {class, representation} and the supplied leaf equality compares `class` alone, byte-for-byte — an implementation that reaches for native object equality instead of the supplied relation fails every case whose representations differ. Struct entries are written as [hexKey, node] pairs in deliberate insertion order; a conforming implementation must accept them in that order and still judge equality order-independently. Every judgment is append-only except an explicit erratum.

cases.name: same-class-different-representation
cases.note: Leaf(x) = Leaf(y) iff x ≈ y — and ≈ is the supplied relation, which ignores representation.

cases.name: distinct-class
cases.note: Same representation is irrelevant; ≈ compares class.

cases.name: empty-leaf-equals-empty-leaf
cases.note: The empty class is a class; ≈ holds between empty classes.

cases.name: empty-leaf-is-not-the-empty-struct
cases.note: Leaf(_) ≠ Struct(_) always. An empty struct is not a leaf carrying something empty.

cases.name: leaf-is-not-a-nonempty-struct
cases.note: Constructor disjointness does not depend on what either side contains.

cases.name: empty-struct-equals-empty-struct
cases.note: dom ∅ = dom ∅, pointwise condition vacuous.

cases.name: empty-key-is-a-key
cases.note: The empty byte string is a legal key like any other.

cases.name: empty-key-entry-is-not-no-entry
cases.note: dom {""} ≠ dom ∅ — a struct with one entry at the empty key has a nonempty domain.

cases.name: key-content-distinguishes
cases.note: Key equality is octet equality; 00 and 01 are different keys.

cases.name: key-length-distinguishes
cases.note: 01 is a prefix of 01 00 and still a different key — length is part of the octets.

cases.name: key-order-within-the-key-matters
cases.note: Same octets, different sequence — different key.

cases.name: insertion-order-is-not-observable
cases.note: Sibling order is not part of a node; keys already distinguish the children.

cases.name: missing-key
cases.note: dom m ≠ dom n — and the judgment is symmetric: extra on one side is missing on the other.

cases.name: same-domain-children-swapped
cases.note: Equality is pointwise at each key, never a multiset comparison of children.

cases.name: nested-empty-structs-differ-from-bare-empty
cases.note: Neither side reaches a leaf; only the interior path at key 61 separates them. Leaf paths alone are not enough.

cases.name: nested-empty-structs-equal-when-domains-agree
cases.note: Pointwise recursion bottoms out at equal empty structs.

cases.name: recursive-pointwise-equality
cases.note: Equality recurses through outer/inner and applies ≈ only at the leaves.

cases.name: recursive-difference-at-depth
cases.note: A single ≈-failure at any depth fails the whole judgment.

cases.name: nested-domains-differ-at-depth
cases.note: Domain comparison applies at every level, not only at the root.

cases.name: leaf-struct-disjointness-at-depth
cases.note: Leaf(_) ≠ Struct(_) holds pointwise under a shared key as surely as at the root.

cases.name: deep-mixed-stressor
cases.note: Everything at once: empty key, insertion-order independence at two levels, representation differences, an interior empty struct.
